title: Warnings
description: Backups that went through but could not back up some items: which ones, why and what to do. Acknowledged warnings no longer count until a new problem appears.
failedHint: {count, plural, one {# protected object or machine has} other {# protected objects or machines have}} a failed last backup. Failed backups cannot be acknowledged; they stay red until a backup succeeds again.
failedGuestsHint: {count, plural, one {# VM or container in a backup job has} other {# VMs or containers in a backup job have}} a failed last backup. Failed backups cannot be acknowledged; they stay red until a backup succeeds again.
loadError: The warnings could not be loaded.

open.title: No open warnings
open.description: The last backups of all protected objects, machines and file shares are complete, or their warnings are acknowledged.

acknowledged.title: No acknowledged warnings
acknowledged.description: Acknowledged warnings appear here, with the person, the time and the note.

failedItems: {count, plural, one {# item not backed up} other {# items not backed up}}
superseded: The acknowledgement of {when} no longer applies, because a new problem appeared since.

reasons.notAllowed: Your role does not allow acknowledging warnings.
reasons.failed: A failed backup cannot be acknowledged. It stays red until a backup succeeds again.
reasons.noWarning: The last backup is complete. There is nothing to acknowledge.
reasons.nothingSelected: Select objects with an open warning first.

dialog.title: {count, plural, one {Acknowledge warning} other {Acknowledge # warnings}}
dialog.description: Acknowledged warnings no longer count in the overview, the status and the protected objects. If a new cause appears or a backup fails, the warning shows again. Failed backups cannot be acknowledged.
dialog.notePlaceholder: For example: the message is damaged at Microsoft, clarified with the person.
dialog.noteHelp: The note is visible to all administrators and is kept in the audit log.

revokeDialog.title: Revoke the acknowledgement?
revokeDialog.description: The warning of {name} then counts again in the overview and the status.

toast.skipped: {count, plural, one {# object was skipped because it no longer has an open warning.} other {# objects were skipped because they no longer have an open warning.}}
toast.failed: That did not work. Please try again.

explain.open: The last backup of {when} went through, but {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} could not be backed up. Everything else is backed up; {appName} tries the affected items again in the next run.
explain.acknowledged: The last backup of {when} did not back up {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}. The causes are acknowledged, so the warning does not count.
explain.failed: The last backup failed. There is no new restore point. The reason is shown with the run below.

detail.title: Backup history and warnings
detail.loadError: The details could not be loaded.
detail.noRuns: There is no run for this object yet.
detail.itemsCapped: Showing the first {shown} of {total} items. The causes above count all of them.
detail.noItems: No individual items are stored for this run.
detail.attempts: {count, plural, one {for the first time} other {in # runs in a row}}

toConfirmHint: {count, plural, one {# object is no longer backed up (removed, disabled, unlicensed or locked) and waits for a confirmation.} other {# objects are no longer backed up (removed, disabled, unlicensed or locked) and wait for a confirmation.}} That is not a failure, but readiness stays yellow until it is confirmed.

held.title: Held backups
held.description: Backups that would leave their storage target too little free space are held before they fill the storage. A backup that adds far more than usual only raises a notice, unless its object's size check is set to "hold": then it is held as well. Every further backup of a held object waits.
held.none: No backup is held. Runs are checked against the free space their storage target keeps (by default 5 % of its size, at least 20 GiB, at most 500 GiB) on targets that report it, and against ten times what their object usually adds, at least 10 GiB: by default a run past that goes on with a notice.

kind.m365: Mailbox, OneDrive, site or IMAP account

why.size: Would add more than {limit}: {bytes} so far, usually {usual}.
why.sizeNoHistory: Would add more than {limit}: {bytes} so far.
why.space: Would leave the storage target too little free space: {free} of {total} free.

held.spaceNote: This hold ends by itself once the target has room again: the next run checks again and goes ahead. It cannot be continued once, since that would fill the target. Free up space on the target, or switch the space rule off for the target or the tenant.
held.refused: {count, plural, one {# later run held} other {# later runs held}}
held.continuesNext: The next run of this object goes through once without the check.
held.excludeHint: If a folder was added by mistake (a recycle bin, a download folder), exclude it in the object's backup settings first.

space.summary: Keeps {percent} % of the target free, at least {min}, at most {max}
space.off: Off: no space is kept free
space.enabled: Keep space free on the storage target
space.targetTitle: Free space on this storage target
space.targetDescription: A backup run is held when it would leave this target less free space than this. Applies to this target only, before the tenant's and the installation's rule. Small targets keep at most a quarter of their size free.
space.installationHint: Applies to every storage target that reports its size and free space, unless a tenant or a target has its own rule. On the shared default target only this rule applies.
space.installationDescription: A backup run is held when it would leave its storage target less free space than this: the share of the target's size, but at least the minimum and at most the maximum. A target that reports free space but no size keeps the minimum. Small targets keep at most a quarter of their size free.
space.tenantTitle: Free space on the storage targets of this tenant
space.shared: This tenant writes to the installation's shared default target, where the installation's rule applies: {rule}.

notices.title: Unusually large backups that went on
notices.description: Runs of the last 30 days that wrote more than their limit. They were not stopped: by default {appName} only warns about large backups.
notices.row: Wrote {bytes}, more than its limit of {limit}
notices.toast: Large runs of this object are held from now on.

actions.switchOff: Switch the check off for this object

raise.title: Raise the limit of {name}
raise.description: The held run had added {bytes}. Each run of this object may then add at least the new limit; ten times its usual stays the rule above it.
raise.label: New limit in GiB

settings.title: Size and space check of backups
settings.description: For every object of this tenant without its own settings. A run that adds more than the factor times the median of its object's last runs (and at least the minimum) raises a notice and goes on, or is held when the size check is set to "hold". A run is always held when it would leave its storage target less free space than the rule below keeps.
settings.enabled: Check the size of backup runs
settings.mode: When a run adds more than that
settings.modeWarn: Notify only, the run goes on (default)
settings.modeHold: Hold the run until an administrator decides
settings.firstRunExempt: empty: first backups are not checked

toast.raised: Limit raised. The next run goes through up to it.
toast.switchedOff: The check is off for this object.
